verdicts.evidence: Unitary DFT on a discrete grid confirms Parseval/inner-product preservation to relative error 1.5e-16 and the pairing identity for both a random density and a Sinkhorn-computed OT coupling to relative gaps 6.6e-16 and 1.4e-15; a non-unitary mutation breaks the identity with gap 1.03e+3.

On a genuine 4-point BOT instance (Birkhoff polytope, 24 permutations) with 60 seeds at T=400, the certified Theorem bound held in 60/60 runs (mean regret 51.29 vs bound 836.04), with sublinear log-log slopes 0.757/0.762 across T up to 6400; Cauchy-noise mutation collapses coverage to 0.00.

Exact LP Kantorovich value vs log-domain Sinkhorn on 40-point OT confirms gap/(ε log(1/ε)) in [0.439, 0.758] across ε sweep; cumulated penalty under ε_t=ηt^{-η} matches T^{1-η} log T shape and is dominated by √T log T; constant-ε mutation yields exactly linear slope 1.0000.

Basis-truncation EntUCB over N∈{2…32}, T∈{250…4000}, 125 runs: bound held in 125/125, stripped log-log slopes are 0.50000 in N and 0.50000 in T; broken-feedback mutation yields linear regret slope 0.984.

Analytic exponent (q+2)/(2q+2) ranges from 0.976 (q=0.05, →O(T)) to 0.515 (q=32, →Õ(√T)); full theorem expression fitted over T∈{10³…10⁶} yields ordered slopes 0.982…0.611 matching the analytic trend; frozen-truncation mutation gives linear slope 0.970.

RLS estimator stationary-point gradient norm 3.8e-10; Sylvester identity for log-det width holds to gap 1.8e-15; coverage 1.000 over 400 runs (d=8, T=300) vs nominal 0.95; shrinking β by 6× collapses coverage to 0.000.

overall: The logbook provides concrete numerical evidence from executed experiments supporting all six claims, with each claim backed by specific quantitative results and a mutation that breaks the expected behavior. All experiments are finite-dimensional/discrete instantiations of the paper's infinite-dimensional theory—a limitation the logbook openly acknowledges—but they use genuine optimal transport problems and actual bandit algorithms rather than proxy tasks.
